name: Sheikh Hasina
role: Prime Minister of Bangladesh (1996–2001, 2009–2024); Awami League president
summary: Hasina led a developmental, nominally secular Awami League government that stressed growth, social safety nets, women's empowerment, climate finance for vulnerable countries and the legacy of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. She pursued war-crimes trials for 1971 collaborators, a hard line on militancy and drugs, and defended the Digital Security Act, while critics accuse her government of authoritarian rule and the July 2024 crackdown. Since her ouster she has called for free elections and denounced the interim government.

universal-healthcare.rationale: At UNGA 2023 she praised Bangladesh's community clinics bringing primary care to the grassroots, backed minimum health-coverage benchmarks and joined the UN universal health coverage meeting.

cut-welfare.rationale: Told the UN she expanded social safety nets (US$12 billion allocated, a new Universal Pension Scheme, coverage for widows, elderly and disabled); she presents this as an achievement.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Launched and defended a hard anti-drug campaign in 2018, promising 'Nobody will be spared however influential he may be'.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Told UNGA she is concerned by misuse of information technology for 'spreading hate speech and inflammatory rhetoric' and that such acts incite violence; she also defended the Digital Security Act.

nation-first.rationale: Urged the UN to 'choose unity, solidarity, and multilateralism over fragmentation, insularity and isolation'.

limit-growth.rationale: Pursues rapid growth (high-income Bangladesh by 2041, 'one of the fastest growing economies') and frames climate response as resilient development, not growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Told the UN 'urgent, bold and ambitious collective actions are needed' on climate and called on major emitters to submit and implement ambitious NDCs.

democracy-best.rationale: Calls her aim an inclusive democracy, but her government held three disputed elections boycotted or contested by the opposition; mixed.

separate-church-state.rationale: Called Bangladesh a 'secular democracy' (2010, 2013) and urged tolerance of every religion, but her government kept Islam as state religion and she accepted removal of a statue under Islamist pressure; mixed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Assured Islamic scholars in 2011 that no law contrary to the Quran would be enacted and revised the women's policy after examining Surah An-Nisa, yet she also rejected a new blasphemy law and describes the country as secular; mixed.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Her stated policy is to eliminate discrimination against women and reach gender equality within a stipulated timeframe, including a 50% participation goal.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Record: no accountability for the Rapid Action Battalion's extrajudicial killings or the 2024 killings of protesters under her government; the record wins.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Told the UN that the constitution guarantees fundamental rights for all, that reforms secured 'equal legal protection and access to justice for everyone', and urged action for equality, justice and freedom for all human beings.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said the people should decide who runs the country, but the 2014, 2018 and 2024 elections under her were widely judged not free and fair; the record wins.

party-controls-media.rationale: Record: her government used the Digital Security Act to arrest journalists and critics and pressured outlets; the record wins.

death-penalty.rationale: Said war-crimes verdicts 'will be executed' (2012) and, as head of the cabinet, had the death penalty extended to all rapes (2020).

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: At UNGA she demanded that developed economies fulfil their 100-billion-dollar climate commitments, back a US$500 billion SDG stimulus and provide concessional finance and support after LDC graduation.

refugee-return.rationale: Called repeatedly for Rohingya refugees to be repatriated to Myanmar, saying they 'want to return to their own country' and live peacefully there.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Stated aim of 50% women's participation in all sectors by 2030 and women's representation at all tiers of government; no explicit quota for public bodies cited.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Said military dictators after 1975 'jeopardised all election process' and that elections were 'just a game' then; her party struggled to restore democracy.

non-intervention.rationale: Demanded that human rights not be politicised 'to put pressure on developing countries' and in 2024 said foreign powers plotted against her; but she also seeks international pressure on Myanmar and supports UN peacekeeping.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Rejected a new blasphemy law as unnecessary but said existing laws are 'enough' to punish anyone who insults religion, and defended arresting bloggers for hurting religious sentiment.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Bangladesh is party to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, which she cited at the UN as part of her government's disarmament record.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Said she could have stayed in power had she allowed a foreign airbase or ceded St Martin's Island, implying she refused to host one.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Insists the 1971 killings (three million dead) be recognised, calling for the 'atrocities and barbarity' of Pakistani forces to be acknowledged and marking 25 March as Genocide Day.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Told parliament independence came by 'shedding blood of millions of martyrs' that must not be in vain; honours the martyrs of 1966 and 1971.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Said in May 2024 that a 'white man's' plot sought to carve a 'Christian country' out of Bangladesh and Myanmar and to topple her government.

future-generations.rationale: Warned climate threatens the security and prosperity of 'present and future generations' and committed Bangladesh to protecting the environment and biodiversity.

arms-reduction.rationale: Told the UN Bangladesh's commitment to 'general and complete disarmament is unwavering' and urged full implementation of disarmament treaties.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for an international financial architecture giving developing countries low-cost funds with minimal conditionality, equitable SDR access and a disaster clause in lending.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: In 2010 reportedly backed equal property rights for women; in April 2011 she said contradictions with the Quran had been removed from the policy after Islamist objections. Mixed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Defines her struggle as free and fair elections, while presiding over elections widely judged neither; mixed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Told the UN she ensured political representation of women at all levels of government 'from the top to the lowest tier'.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Defended the 2018 drug campaign saying deaths came in 'gunfights' that 'naturally occur' when suspects fire, and said misdeeds in raids would be tried; she did not endorse killing without trial, but rights groups call the deaths extrajudicial.

notes: Open full-text sources were mostly news reprints of speeches; many topics (economic policy details, religion and family law, nuclear power, China and India ties) lacked her own words and are left null. Her handling of 2024 protest deaths is contested and only her own statements are used.
